name: neuroinfections overview
title: Suspected meningitis or encephalitis: blood culture and empiric treatment first, CT before the lumbar puncture only with focal signs or a decreased level of consciousness, then the CSF separates bacterial meningitis, aseptic (viral) meningitis and herpes simplex encephalitis, each with its organisms and treatment

root.title: Fever · headache · stiff neck · altered mental status: think MENINGITIS
lines: classic triad: FEVER, ALTERED MENTAL STATUS, NUCHAL RIGIDITY (Kernig's, Brudzinski's)
language trouble, confusion, focal seizures → think ENCEPHALITIS (the brain itself)

groups.title: Suspected CNS infection: treat FIRST, then let the CSF decide

pres.title: Plan
lines: 2 · START EMPIRIC treatment now: never wait for the CT or the tap
3 · CT/MRI FIRST only if focal signs or ↓ consciousness (PUNISH: Papilledema, Unconscious, Neurologic deficit, Immunocompromised, Seizure, History of CNS disease) → mass = NEUROSURGERY
4 · LUMBAR PUNCTURE → adjust treatment to the CSF

head: h
Bacterial meningitis
any age · a clinical EMERGENCY
csf: • adults: S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae
• neonates: E. coli, group B strep
tx: • + AMPICILLIN 2 g q4h if > 50 or immunocompromised
with the FIRST antibiotic dose, then q6h for 4 days

head: h
Herpes simplex encephalitis
the BRAIN itself · MESIAL TEMPORAL lobes
clue: • focal seizures, impaired memory, focal deficits
• fever, ↓ awareness · usually NO stiff neck
